en.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Live-Action Film Won't Adapt Game, CD Projekt Red Confirms
en.summary: Forget a direct retelling of V's journey. CD Projekt Red has officially confirmed that the upcoming live-action Cyberpunk 2077 movie will forge its own path, exploring new stories within the beloved dystopian universe.
en.body:
Night City is expanding its horizons beyond the screen and into live-action, but don't expect to relive the exact chrome-plated chaos of **Cyberpunk 2077**. CD Projekt Red has made it clear that the upcoming film adaptation, in partnership with Paramount and produced by **Lorenzo di Bonaventura** (known for his work on the *Transformers* franchise), aims to tell a *new* story within the established universe.

Co-CEO **Michał Nowakowski** stated, "At this point, we can only say that we definitely don't want to make a film adaptation of the game. We want to tell a story in the world of Cyberpunk, but it won't be a one-to-one translation of the game's story." This approach is a welcome sign for fans who have seen how well original narratives can flourish within established IPs, much like the critically acclaimed anime series **Cyberpunk: Edgerunners**.

## A Universe Ripe for New Tales

The decision not to directly adapt the game's narrative allows for incredible creative freedom. The world of **Cyberpunk 2077**, originally conceived by tabletop RPG designer **Mike Pondsmith**, is a sprawling, complex tapestry filled with compelling themes. It delves into identity, autonomy, and the very nature of self in an age of pervasive cybernetic modification. This fertile ground is perfect for exploring the lives of new characters, perhaps delving into the pre-Johnny Silverhand era or showcasing the myriad of subcultures and corporate machinations that define Night City. The success of **Cyberpunk: Edgerunners**, which introduced compelling original characters like David Martinez and Lucy Lustrous while staying true to the game's aesthetic and thematic core, serves as a strong precedent for this multimedia expansion.

## What This Means for Fans

For the passionate global fanbase of **Cyberpunk 2077**, this news is an exciting prospect. Instead of a potentially condensed or altered version of V's journey, players and viewers can anticipate a fresh narrative that enriches the existing lore. This allows for the exploration of different facets of Night City, potentially featuring new gangs, corporate intrigue, or even a deeper dive into the philosophical quandaries that make the **Cyberpunk** universe so captivating. It’s an opportunity to see the world through a different lens, offering new perspectives on themes of transhumanism and societal decay that are central to the franchise's appeal. The fact that CD Projekt Red is taking a similar approach to its successful anime venture suggests a well-thought-out strategy for expanding the **Cyberpunk** brand across different media.

## What's Next

While details about the plot, cast, and director for the live-action **Cyberpunk 2077** movie have not yet been announced, the confirmation of a new story bodes well for the franchise's future. Paramount is also developing other major video game adaptations, including films for **Street Fighter** and **Call of Duty**, indicating a significant push into the gaming space. Fans will be eagerly awaiting further announcements regarding this ambitious project.

content_raw: CD Projekt Red has finally spoken up about the live-action Cyberpunk 2077 movie . The company said it doesn’t want to do a 1:1 adaptation of the game, instead telling a new story within the same universe. "At this point, we can only say that we definitely don't want to make a film adaptation of the game," co-CEO Michał Nowakowski told Polish outlet PAP Biznes , via GamesRadar . "We want to tell a story in the world of Cyberpunk, but it won't be a one-to-one translation of the game's story." The Cyberpunk movie is being created in partnership with Parmount, now under the Skydance banner after the recent merger . The film will be produced by Lorenzo di Bonaventura, of live-action Transformers fame. It’ll be interesting to see how far the movie strays from the game, which featured a freelance mercenary called V who put a mysterious computer chip in their brain and ended up haunted by the digital ghost of Keanu Reeves’ Johnny Silverhand. I’d personally love them to go back, get Reeves back in, and tell Silverhand’s story before he ended up stuck in a chip. Of course, the Cyberpunk universe — created by tabletop RPG designer Mike Pondsmith — is wide enough to tell a range of original stories. It’s fertile soil for pulling at themes of identity, autonomy, and the self as a ship of theseus to be modified and reprinted. It sounds like a similar approach the company took to anime. Cyberpunk: Edgerunners feels like a faithful multimedia project within the world CDPR created — featuring locations and characters from the game world — but it tells a fresh story about original characters in its dystopian posthuman hellscape. The Studio Trigger-led anime series is back on Netflix this month when Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 launches on October 20. Check out the IGN interview with the creators of Edgerunners for the lowdown. CD Projekt also recently announced that work has officially begun on Project Hadar , its first game in its own original universe. The company has previously only played in the worlds of others, with The Witcher based on novels and Cyberpunk based on a tabletop RPG. Elsewhere in CD Project Land, The Witcher 3 just got a remaster on consoles and PC, which saw the iconic RPG get a makeover. There were some issues with the new visuals, particularly heavy bloom in The Witcher 3 remaster , but CDPR was on the case quickly. And of course, Cyberpunk 2 is in the works, although it feels years away.
